requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
I found no gap. Each obligation in `requirements.ci.span` has code reachable from the `{impl}` item and a `{test}`-referenced test.

**Implementation.** The only `{impl}` is the comment in `src/evidence.rs` `fn[collect_definitions]` on the body-text computation. It reaches `definition_blocks`, `colon_fence` and `without_options` in `src/lib.rs`, so none of those needs its own reference.

**Obligations, code and tests**

| Obligation | Code | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Opening fence of at least three colons, immediately followed by `{req} <name>` | `colon_fence` returns the suffix only when it has at least 3 colons. `definition_blocks` strips the `{req}` prefix from that suffix. | `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent` in `src/lib.rs` rejects `::{req}`, `::: {req}` and `:::{req}ready`. `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` covers a four-colon opener. |
| Closing fence has at least as many colons as the opener and nothing else but whitespace | `definition_blocks` finds the first later line with `colon_fence` count ≥ the opener's and `suffix.trim().is_empty()`. | The same `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text…` test: `:::foo` does not close and `::: ` does. `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` and `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` (`src/evidence.rs`) cover a shorter nested fence and a missing closer. |
| Fences MAY be indented up to three spaces; four or more MUST NOT be a fence | `colon_fence` returns `None` when more than 3 leading spaces are stripped. | The same test covers indented open and close fences, a four-space opener that is not a block, and a four-space closer that leaves the block unclosed. |
| Body is all Markdown between the fence lines (headings, examples, diagrams, blank lines) | `body_start` is the end of the opening line and `body_end` is the start of the closing line. Fence-like lines inside Markdown code blocks are skipped through `overlaps_protected` and `code_block_ranges`. | `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` uses a body with a fenced code block containing `:::`, ATX and Setext headings, and blank lines. `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` covers a code example in the body. |
| Body does not include text after the closing fence | `end` and `body_end` stop at the closing line. | The same span test has "Outside the requirement." and a following requirement. `a_longer_colon_fence…` asserts the outside text is not in the body. |
| Leading and trailing whitespace excluded when comparing with evidence | `.trim()` in `collect_definitions`. | `requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace`. |

**Option lines.** `without_options` removes `:impl:`/`:test:` option lines from the body text. That is not stated in `requirements.ci.span`, but `requirements.references.anchors` specifies it: "Option lines MUST NOT form part of the definition's text". I did not treat it as unspecified behavior. `collect_definitions` carries no `{impl}` for that requirement, but this is a note on the anchors requirement, not a gap in the span subject.

No `{fixme}` references are involved.

text: :::{req} span

A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
